maria_capacity: Quick capacity check — p99 latency for /generate is popping >350ms during morning spike. We hit 96 GPUs and queue depth climbs.
alex_ops: What SLO are we targeting again? p95 120ms, p99 250ms right?
maria_capacity: Correct. p95=120ms, p99=250ms. Did a back-of-envelope using Erlang C and simple M/M/c assumptions. Sharing numbers.
maria_capacity: ```
assumptions:
  req_rate = 220 req/s (observed peak today)
  avg_service_time = 0.6s per req on a single GPU (incl kv cache miss avg)
  mu = 1/0.6 = 1.667 req/s per GPU
  c = current_gpus = 96
  utilization rho = req_rate / (c * mu) = 220 / (96*1.667) = ~0.137
Erlang C gives P(queue) ~ 0.02 -> avg wait ~ 0.02 * (1/(c*mu - lambda)) ~ small
But tail dominated by short high-latency outliers from 3 nodes with degraded NVLINK and a 10% cpu throttling event.
Result: theoretical p99 ~ 180ms if all nodes healthy, observed p99 ~ 350ms due to node variance and small burstiness.
``` 
sam_sre: Nice. So the model says capacity ok in steady-state but real-world variance kills the tail. Can we either a) add headroom or b) tighten admission control to keep p99? 
jen_prod: Adding GPUs costs $Xk/mo. How much headroom do we need for 99% SLO with 20% burst? 
maria_capacity: With 20% burst -> req_rate=264 req/s. Recompute: rho=264/(96*1.667)=0.165. The ErlangC p(queue) increases but still low. However to bound p99 < 250ms across node variance we need effective c~=120 (adding 25% GPUs) OR reduce avg_service_time by 15% (quantization / batching improvements).
alex_ops: If we do admission control, what policy? global token-bucket? per-route concurrency limit? We prefer graceful degradation over hard rejects.
maria_capacity: Proposal: two-layer admission control:
  - global soft concurrency cap that starts shedding at 220 req/s (10% above current steady) using `505` responses with Retry-After for non-critical routes
  - per-model max concurrent per-GPU to keep per-GPU queue < 4
  - emergency hard-shed at 300 req/s (protect platform)
Small snippet for rate limiter config:
```
route: /generate
  token_bucket: capacity=300, refill=50/s
  concurrency_limit: 4 per GPU
  soft_shed_threshold: 220
  hard_shed_threshold: 300
```
sam_sre: I like soft shed + canary rollout. Also add health-weighted routing so nodes with degraded perf get lower load.
jen_prod: For procurement, if we choose +25% GPUs (96->120) what's monthly delta? approx +24 GPUs -> ~ $6k-10k/mo depending on instance. Add networking & amp.
maria_capacity: Actionable options:
  A) Short term: deploy admission control config, add health-weighted routing, enable per-node backoff — low cost, deploy this week
  B) Mid term: enable faster kernels / 8-bit quant -> 15% service time reduction (2-4 weeks)
  C) Long term: procure +25% reserved capacity for Q3 seasonal headroom (decision in 2 weeks)
capacity-bot: Reminder: existing reserved capacity contract renewal window opens in 18 days.
alex_ops: I'll own option A (work with eng-runtime). Sam will own health routing changes.
sam_sre: Will roll health-weighted routing today, and add a dashboard for node-latency variance.
jen_prod: I'll run cost projection for +25% and check budget signoff timelines.
maria_capacity: Thanks. One more note: p99 is sensitive to tail from a few bad nodes — prioritize quickly removing those from rotation when NVLINK errors detected. Add auto-drain on node_degraded events.
alex_ops: +1 on auto-drain.
maria_capacity: I'll post follow-up with exact ErlangC numbers and simulation traces tomorrow. For now, plan = A short-term + health routing, then measure; we revisit procurement if still >250ms p99.
sam_sre: Sounds good :thumbsup:
